source.title: PolySAE: Modeling Feature Interactions in Sparse Autoencoders via Polynomial Decoding
source.authors: Panagiotis Koromilas; A. Demou; James Oldfield; Yannis Panagakis; M. Nicolaou

record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates sparse-autoencoder features in real language models, bearing on the indirect-evidence version, but does not reproduce toy-model superposition experiments or measure feature-overlap geometry.
record.gate_note: The paper cites superposition as motivation for SAEs and relies on sparse dictionary learning, but does not test whether extra sparse features are stored as overlapping directions, whether features are dropped, or how geometry varies with sparsity or importance. Rows cover semantic probing of SAE representations and the paper's evidence that interaction terms capture compositional content beyond individual SAE features. Cited findings from other work are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: PolySAE is a new SAE architecture. All results compare PolySAE with vanilla SAEs: probing F1, Wasserstein separation, interaction interpretability and steering rank. The paper uses superposition and SAEs as motivation and tooling. It does not measure whether models store features in superposition, how features are spread across neurons, or whether SAE features are complete, stable or canonical units. Its argument that linear SAEs conflate atomic and compositional features bears on V5 only indirectly. That argument rests mainly on the method comparison and selected qualitative examples, so it is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that PolySAE adds low-rank pairwise and triple interaction terms to the decoder while keeping a linear encoder. It improves probing F1 by about 8% on average at comparable reconstruction and CE recovery, and gives 2–10× larger Wasserstein separation. Its interaction weights are essentially uncorrelated with co-occurrence (r=0.06 vs 0.82 for SAE covariance), and the learned directions causally steer outputs toward compositional targets. Correction: 'weakly related' should read 'negligibly correlated'. The paper presents compositional structure as largely independent of surface statistics.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains and evaluates polynomial-decoder SAEs on language-model activations; it does not reproduce the original toy-network method or test its superposition geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by model and sparsification strategy; the reported aggregate probing gain is small for Gemma2-2b with TopK.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors argue linear SAE decoders cannot represent nonlinear composition, forcing monolithic features for compounds like 'Starbucks'. Evidence: PolySAE raises single-feature probing F1 (~8% average) at comparable MSE. Selected examples show vanilla SAE activating broad or unrelated features where PolySAE pairs capture the composite. Vanilla SAE covariance tracks co-occurrence (r=0.82); PolySAE interaction weights barely do (r=0.06).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linear SAE dictionaries conflate atomic and compositional features, so individual SAE features are not clean atomic units of the model's representation. This is evidenced by gains from modeling multiplicative feature interactions in the decoder.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The paper evaluates models only up to 2B parameters and restricts experiments to forced-sparsity SAE variants. The interaction interpretability estimate uses a GPT-4o-mini judge on 70K selected pairs; selected qualitative examples do not establish generality. No direct test of superposition geometry is performed.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 reports separate F1 and Wasserstein results for each dataset, model, and sparsifier. These dataset-level cells are not separately extracted; the per-model, per-sparsifier mean F1 results are recorded in r1-r12. No other claim-relevant result rows were omitted.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity transitions or feature geometry.
No capacity or importance analysis of polysemantic neurons.
No analysis of alternative causes of polysemanticity.
No measure of how features are distributed across neurons. No test that SAEs recover the model's true features: SAEs serve only as a tool and comparator.

No direct test of completeness, stability across seeds or sizes, or canonicity of SAE features. The compositional-structure argument rests on comparisons with the authors' own method and selected examples.
Not tested. Multi-dimensional features are mentioned only via a citation (Engels et al.).

record.verdict_notes: Method paper. The reader's V4 'supports' and V5 'challenges' labels are withdrawn: every row compares the authors' PolySAE with vanilla SAEs or rates PolySAE's own interactions. Steering (27 concepts, 324 prompts), direction alignment (cosine 0.372 vs 0.311) and Table 3 concentration results are also own-method comparisons and not claim-relevant. Superposition is cited only as motivation (Elhage et al., 2022), not tested.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, more sparse features than dimensions, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether polysemanticity results from competition for capacity, or whether feature importance determines dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Whether polysemanticity arises from mechanisms other than capacity pressure.

The paper tests whether SAE-derived sparse representations carry semantic signal, but does not measure how broadly features are distributed across neurons or establish that SAE features recover the model's native features.

The paper examines whether additive SAE features capture compositional meanings completely in selected cases. It does not test feature stability across settings or whether SAE features are canonical units generally.
Whether the model's underlying features are intrinsically one-dimensional or multidimensional.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small
rows.operation_detail: Assess selected learned feature interactions for compositional interpretability using GPT-4o-mini.

conditions.value: 70K evaluated from 292,361 pairs with non-negligible interaction strength

rows.measure: Interactions scoring above 0.9 for matching the composite concept
rows.note: The paper also gives selected qualitative comparisons in which interaction terms represent compositions that vanilla SAE features do not capture specifically. The judge result covers a selected subset and does not assess stability or canonicity.
rows.check: This is an interpretability rate of the study's own PolySAE interaction terms, judged by GPT-4o-mini. It has no baseline and no measure of vanilla SAE feature completeness, stability or canonicity, so it does not test V5.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports

reader_labels.reason: SAE representations yield semantic probing signal, and PolySAE mean F1 exceeds the vanilla SAE comparator in all 12 configurations; rows r1-r12.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Selected GPT-2 Small Top-K compositional interactions
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports interpretable interaction-level compositions beyond what individual vanilla SAE features capture in selected examples, qualifying the claim that SAE features alone are complete units; the scaled judge assessment found 12% above 0.9. Row r13.
